source: A. D. Dupuis and W. Hathaway, Aeroballistic Range Tests of the Basic Finner Reference Projectile at Supersonic Velocities, DREV-TM-9703, Defence Research Establishment Valcartier, August 1997 (DTIC ADA636861): Table IX, 'Six-degree-of freedom aerodynamic coefficients - Multiple fits' (PDF pp. 48-49), Fig. 2, 'Model configuration' (PDF p. 53), and sections 3.1 (the model, PDF p. 16) and 5.2 (the fits and the moment reference, PDF pp. 22-23). Crown copyright (Canada); approved for public release, distribution unlimited (THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md). The values are typed here in the project's own layout; no text, figure or scan is copied.
reading: Typed from the printed table, each cell checked against a 110-dpi render of the page. Each row is one multiple fit: two to four free flights at one nominal Mach number reduced together by a six-degree-of-freedom fit, given at their average mid-range Mach number. cn_alpha is the table's CNa and cm_alpha its Cma, the linear terms of the normal-force and pitching-moment coefficients, per radian (the report's derivatives are with respect to the sine of the angle of attack), on the body's cross-section pi d^2/4, the moment about the reference point 5.50 calibers aft of the nose tip (section 5.2). The report's nomenclature gives the reference area and states no reference length; the body's diameter d is taken (ADR-351). cn_alpha_probable_error_percent and cm_alpha_probable_error_percent are the fit's probable errors as the table prints them, in whole percent (the table prints '0.%' for the moment's). The fits' cubic terms, CNa3 and Cma3, are both held at 0 on these six rows (the table solves for Cma3 only at its two rows above Mach 3.5), so each slope is a linear fit over the angles flown. mean_squared_yaw_deg2 is the table's DBSQ, the fit's mean squared yaw in square degrees. The two rows above Mach 3.5 (3.734 and 4.300) are outside the project's envelope and are not typed. source_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the PDF the cells were typed from, pinned as `drev-tm-9703` in validation/refs.lock.toml; typed_on is the date they were typed.

geometry.note: Fig. 2, in calibers of the body's diameter, 30.0 mm: a cone of 10 degrees half-angle 2.84 calibers long on a cylinder, 10.0 calibers overall; four rectangular fins 1.0 caliber in chord and 1.0 in span, flush with the base; each fin drawn as a single wedge in section, sharp at the leading edge (radius 0.004) and 0.08 calibers thick at its trailing edge (section 3.1 calls the fins 'conical in shape with a thickness of 0.08 cal at the base'), canted 0, 2 or 4 degrees; the nose tip's radius 0.004; the center of gravity 5.50 calibers from the nose tip.

drag_and_damping_source: The same report's Table IX (PDF pp. 48-49) for each row's C_X0 and C_mq, Table VIII, 'Six-degree-of freedom aerodynamic coefficients - Single fit' (PDF pp. 44-46), for each of the row's shots, and Table V, 'Range conditions' (PDF p. 41), for each shot's Reynolds number; section 5.2 (PDF pp. 22-23) and eq. [1] of section 7.0 (PDF p. 28).
drag_and_damping_reading: Typed on 2026-11-16 from the same PDF, each cell checked against a 130-dpi render of its page. cx0 is the table's CX, the axial-force coefficient at zero angle of attack, on pi d^2/4. Table IX prints a probable error under it only at Mach 1.077 and 1.293 ('0.%'); at the other four rows it prints '(*)', a coefficient held in the multiple fit, because each shot of those groups was given its own C_X0 (section 5.2): cx0_fitted_in_the_row is false there, and each shot's single-fit C_X0 and its probable error (all printed '0.%') are typed under shots. cmq is the table's Cmq, the pitch-damping coefficient about the same reference point, with its printed probable error in whole percent. Eq. [1] gives the yaw damping rate as rho A/(4m) times (-C_N_alpha (1 - 1/sigma) + (k2^-2/2)(1 + 1/sigma) C_Mq + ...); with no spin the two arms' rates are each rho A/(4m) (-C_N_alpha + k2^-2 C_Mq/2), which is the linear motion's damping with the rate made dimensionless by q d/(2V), so cmq is per radian of q d/(2V) (an inference: the report states no denominator). A free flight's fit cannot part C_mq from C_m_alpha_dot, so cmq stands for their sum. reynolds_on_length is Table V's, on the model's length, 10 d.
